name: sdlc
conclusion_quantitative: sdlc (Ask) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 7 autonomy limits, 10+ clarification rules, 7 approval gates, 3 validation rules, 9 escalation rules. Strongest: clarification rules.
conclusion_qualitative: sdlc guides the user through an egg SDLC pipeline: gathering the task, refining it, submitting it, monitoring the agents and brokering human-in-the-loop decisions until completion. It keeps questions to a minimum, detecting and inferring what it can, but relays every agent question and phase gate to the human. Cancellations and any destructive recommendation need the human's explicit decision. Alerts, stalls and failures are reported with options for the user, and the agent confirms a pipeline has truly stopped before closing it out.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 7 autonomy limits (7 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly prose.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 7 rules, all strict, 2 tied to a situation, mostly running text. The front matter limits the agent to monitoring tools, read-only `gh` and `git remote` commands, `AskUserQuestion` and the egg pipeline tools. It never asks for the repository when it can detect it, gathers JIRA context without user interaction, continues with the raw ticket ID if JIRA fails, skips the pre-submit confirmation when nothing needed clarifying, and auto-answers decisions the user already answered at an earlier gate.

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ clarification rules (9 mandatory, 1 advisory; 4 conditional), mostly list.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), 9 strict and 1 counted as a suggestion (it contains "may"), 4 tied to a situation, evenly split between running text and bullet points. The agent aims for zero questions, at most one to get started: it asks for the repository only when detection fails, asks one combined question when no task was given, and offers to help scope it with 1 to 2 follow-ups. It asks 1 to 3 targeted questions when the task is ambiguous, asks for a branch qualifier when the name exists, and relays the pipeline agents' questions to the user.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 7 approval gates (7 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 7 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The agent confirms the refined task with the user before submitting, and confirms before cancelling or cancelling and retrying a pipeline. Destructive recommendations are never carried out automatically: only the human authorizes cancellation, phase restarts or other irreversible steps. Each phase ends at a human-in-the-loop gate that the operator approves, sends back for changes or redirects.

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 3 validation rules (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly list.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 3 rules, all strict, 2 tied to a situation, all bullet points. Before treating a failed pipeline as finished the agent confirms through a pipeline snapshot that it has really stopped, and before rescuing work it verifies the branch has commits.

Only exit to Phase 5 when `status` is `failed`, `running_agents` is empty, **and** the secondary check confirms the pipeline is genuinely stopped.
Verify branch has commits: `git log --oneline origin/egg/<branch> ^origin/main`

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 9 escalation rules (8 mandatory, 1 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly list.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 9 rules, 8 strict and 1 counted as a suggestion (it contains "recommended"), 2 tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The agent tells the user when the JIRA lookup fails, when a branch already exists, or when status polling hits a permanent error, never retrying silently. Overseer alerts, unresolved review rejections blocking consensus and long-running phases go to the user to decide; stuck pipelines get rescue options, and it reports incomplete rescues and failed cancellations.
